Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF CLoyp A. McIivaIne From ComMpuLsory RETIREMENT
FoR AGE

WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Cloyd A. Mc-
Ilvaine, Executive Secretary, The Panama Canal, who, during the month of February,
1939, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the
service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a
period of one year:

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in
me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S. C., title 5, sec.
715a), I hereby exempt the said Cloyd A. McIlvaine from compulsory retirement for
age for a period of one year ending February 29, 1940.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The only operative command of EO 8025 is its operative paragraph, which exempts Cloyd A. McIlvaine from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending February 29, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires exempting Cloyd A. McIlvaine, who, during the month of February, 1939, "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service". The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on February 29, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later event is recorded for this clause: no held order text revokes, amends, extends or otherwise cites this order (see the earlier-end check).
